games.title: Language Choice
games.description: Choose the form that makes the unit language accurate.

rounds.prompt: In The Hall of One Step, what does the carved phrase say about power?
choices: Power belongs to the tallest building.
Power grows out of wealth and trade.
Power is not in height; one step is a phase.
Power is measured by counting the steps.
rounds.answer: Power is not in height; one step is a phase.
rounds.explanation: The carving separates power from height entirely, which is why Nora reads the hall as a place built for thinking.

rounds.prompt: Which modal verb makes the strongest recommendation in a persuasive letter?
rounds.answer: must
rounds.explanation: Must states an obligation, while might, could and may only offer a possibility.

rounds.prompt: Which sentence uses formal register for a letter to the headteacher?
choices: We can't wait for the garden to be ready!
I am writing to request a garden behind the science block.
You guys should totally come along on Friday.
It's gonna be the best thing our school has ever done.
rounds.answer: I am writing to request a garden behind the science block.
rounds.explanation: Formal register avoids contractions and slang, so only the second option suits a letter to a headteacher.

games.title: Reading Detective
games.description: Use unit evidence to solve each reading clue.

rounds.prompt: In “Save Our School Garden!”, what does the writer say the patch behind the science block looks like now?
choices: The writer says it is only dust and stones, with nothing growing on it.
Each class donates soil or seeds, teachers give one hour a week, and parents lend tools or farming experience.
They think it could be the entrance, even though Nora warns it might only be a goat trap.
rounds.answer: The writer says it is only dust and stones, with nothing growing on it.
rounds.explanation: The opening paragraph contrasts today's dust and stones with the imagined garden of vegetables, herbs and flowers.

rounds.prompt: The text claims emotive language works better than numbers. What reason does it give?
choices: Each class donates soil or seeds, teachers give one hour a week, and parents lend tools or farming experience.
She says the hall was built for thinking, and that its makers taught that every stage of life is a phase.
It says feelings stay in the memory far longer than numbers do.
rounds.answer: It says feelings stay in the memory far longer than numbers do.
rounds.explanation: The reason is about memory, not truth, which is why the text still insists that evidence must sit beside the feeling.

rounds.prompt: How does Nora explain the carved phrase “Power is not in height. One step is a phase.”?
choices: She says understanding is never finished: it is hard work, it changes, and still it lasts.
She says the hall was built for thinking, and that its makers taught that every stage of life is a phase.
A fact can be checked and proved, while an opinion is only what somebody believes or feels.
rounds.answer: She says the hall was built for thinking, and that its makers taught that every stage of life is a phase.
rounds.explanation: Nora reads the carving as an idea about growth rather than architecture, which reframes the whole legend.

games.title: Question Quest
games.description: Read each unit question carefully and choose the best answer.

rounds.prompt: Complete the sentence: Amal has lived in Lomi ______ 2021.
rounds.answer: since
rounds.explanation: The year 2021 names the starting point of the situation, and a starting point always takes since.

rounds.prompt: Which phrase places the adjectives in the natural English order?
rounds.answer: an ancient round grey stone
rounds.explanation: English orders adjectives by age, then shape, then colour, which gives ancient, round, grey.

rounds.prompt: Which line from the story is a simile?
choices: Ideas moved like a telegraph, quiet but fast.
The hall stood magnificent and tall.
rounds.answer: Ideas moved like a telegraph, quiet but fast.
rounds.explanation: A simile compares two unlike things with like or as, and only the first line makes that comparison.

games.title: Unit Mission
games.description: Finish with a mixed challenge across the whole unit.

rounds.prompt: Which sentence from the school garden poster is a fact rather than an opinion?
choices: The patch of land sits behind the science block.
A garden would make our school more magnificent.
The garden is the best idea for our school this year.
Gardening is far more enjoyable than reading indoors.
rounds.answer: The patch of land sits behind the science block.
rounds.explanation: Only the first statement can be checked by walking outside; the other three describe what somebody feels.

rounds.prompt: Which word names the study of how living bodies work?
rounds.answer: physiology
rounds.explanation: Physiology studies how bodies function; a telegraph sends messages, a ceremony marks an event and a descent is a way down.

rounds.prompt: Which sentence uses the present perfect correctly?
rounds.answer: She has finished her poster.
rounds.explanation: She takes has, and the verb must be the past participle finished, so only the second option is correct.
